{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZkNdvw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDK1gM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 91, "title": "Apply the preceding S-DSP envelope to voice output and register snapshots", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `9c7d3f08a8fb6d4d36bb1ef1226ee2415d6efab1`, `Dsp::sample` updates the committed envelope before computing voice output, ENVX and OUTX. Live GAIN changes, rate events and release therefore affect output one sample earlier than the documented voice sequence.

This is the incomplete behavior prioritized by `latest_assessment`, rather than a regression attributed to #89. The supplied context lists no open duplicate Issue.

Concrete evidence:

- [`dsp.rs`, envelope update and output](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/9c7d3f08a8fb6d4d36bb1ef1226ee2415d6efab1/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs#L205): envelope commitment precedes multiplication by `v.env` and register publication.
- [`dsp_hidden_envelope.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/9c7d3f08a8fb6d4d36bb1ef1226ee2415d6efab1/crates/snes-core/tests/dsp_hidden_envelope.rs) and [`dsp_envelope_tests.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/9c7d3f08a8fb6d4d36bb1ef1226ee2415d6efab1/crates/snes-core/src/dsp_envelope_tests.rs) explicitly expect same-call audio changes.
- [#75 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/9c7d3f08a8fb6d4d36bb1ef1226ee2415d6efab1/docs/issue-75-validation.md#implemented-operation-order) acknowledges the retained ordering. [#89 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/9c7d3f08a8fb6d4d36bb1ef1226ee2415d6efab1/docs/issue-89-validation.md#hardware-stages-and-this-cores-call-convention) additionally folds the fifth silent call's envelope update into call six.

## Expected outcome

Implement the preceding-envelope relationship within the existing sample-level DSP API, including its necessary KON initialization boundary.

Hardware basis:

- [Anomie/jwdonal S-DSP documentation, revision 1212](https://gist.github.com/nyanpasu64/a0d916ce6924912a7116682bf778e9a0#file-apudsp_jwdonal-txt), **SOUND GENERATION**, places envelope application and the next voice's modulation input before envelope updating in S3c. S6–S9 describe OUTX/ENVX preparation and publication. **BRR DECODING**, KON sequence #5–#6, starts envelope updating during the fifth silent sample, followed by the first data output.
- [Shay Green's research implementation, mirrored `SPC_DSP.cpp`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/snes9xgit/snes9x/master/apu/bapu/dsp/SPC_DSP.cpp), **V3c, V7–V9**, corroborates capturing output and ENVX from the pre-update envelope, then running the envelope for the next sample. Use this as research corroboration, not imported implementation or an output oracle; record an immutable revision for implementation evidence.
- [Fullsnes ADSR/GAIN documentation](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm#snesapudspadsrgainenvelope) supplies arithmetic and rate context. Retain #75's documented reconciliation of hidden candidates, unsigned bent-GAIN comparison and phase tracking; this Issue changes application order, not those resolved rules.

For ordinary active processing, distinguish `E_apply` from the subsequently committed `E_next`. Compute `O = ((source * E_apply) >> 11) & !1`; use that same O for OUTX, adjacent-voice PMON, dry mixing and EON sends. The end-of-call ENVX snapshot is `E_apply >> 4`, OUTX is O's high byte, while internal envelope state has advanced to `E_next`.

Map KON calls explicitly: retain five zero PCM/ENVX/OUTX calls and the three preload groups/window selection from #89; perform the initial envelope update on call five so call six can consume it. Do not introduce an extra silent call.

Collapsing publication into end-of-call snapshots remains an API convention. It does not establish physical S7/S8/S9 access timing.

## Context and reproduction

Use original public-API vectors with NON enabled, noise rate zero, echo disabled, and voice/master volumes 64 on both channels. The repository's held noise seed yields source −32768, O = −16E and stereo PCM = −4E. Warm the voice before changing registers.

Independently derived discriminators:

| Operation | Correct first affected call | Following call |
| --- | --- | --- |
| From settled direct GAIN 94 (`E=1504`), write GAIN 96 | PCM `(−6016,−6016)`, ENVX 94, OUTX 162; commit E=1536 | PCM `(−6144,−6144)`, ENVX 96, OUTX 160 |
| From E=1504 with held H=1536, select bent GAIN rate 31 | PCM `(−6016,−6016)`, ENVX 94, OUTX 162; commit E=1512 | Apply E=1512, producing PCM `(−6048,−6048)` and OUTX 161 |
| From settled E=16, assert KOFF | PCM `(−64,−64)`, ENVX 1, OUTX 255; commit E=8 | PCM `(−32,−32)`, ENVX 0, OUTX 255; then zero output on the next call |

The baseline instead applies the new commitment immediately. Also cover signed, constant filter-0 BRR at zero pitch to distinguish envelope timing from changing waveform position.

A startup discriminator must cross a real rate boundary: with the existing initial counter convention, linear-increase GAIN rate 29 (`$DD`) has an event on KON call five. Call five remains externally zero while committing E=32; call six applies E=32. This rejects both the baseline's deferred initialization and a blanket extra-sample delay.

**Scope:** ordinary GAIN/ADSR/release output ordering, ENVX/OUTX snapshots, necessary fifth-call initialization, and consumers of the resulting voice output. Keep existing scalar terminal-header and reset conventions explicitly bounded; do not turn this into a header-fetch correction.

**Non-goals and remaining work:** full DSP subcycle scheduling, SPC instruction bus timing, key polling phase, torn writes, live KON-delay directory selection, final pre-KON output/filter retention, physical terminal-header lookahead, writable-register publication races, exhaustive envelope transitions, and physical reset retention. Existing NON advancement disputes remain unresolved.

Planning was read-only. No suites were rerun; numerical examples are specification-derived expectations, not hardware captures.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the bounded ordering correction and fifth-call initialization. Document the call mapping and distinguish applied, hidden and next committed envelopes. Correct the superseded #75/#89 ordering statements while retaining their historical evidence.
- [ ] Add original tests in `crates/snes-core/tests/dsp_envelope_order.rs` covering the numerical anchors above, positive/negative filter-0 sources, direct/dynamic GAIN, ADSR attack/decay/sustain events and holds, release through zero, retrigger and voice isolation. Assert exact PCM/ENVX/OUTX before, on and after changes. Include startup rate-boundary coverage.
- [ ] Run the new public tests against the exact baseline and implementation; record behavioral failures and corrected passes. Expectations must be independently calculated, without production arithmetic generating expected results or another emulator supplying traces.
- [ ] Add or extend a bounded original SPC700 guest uploaded through the firmware-free protocol. Exercise `$F2/$F3` writes/readback with independently derived register and PCM checkpoints. Document its whole-instruction timing assumptions; do not claim physical write-edge accuracy. Record source/data authorship and licensing in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`.
- [ ] Verify whole versus irregular APU tick partitions across live changes, retrigger and a shared-counter wrap, comparing every PCM sample, DSP register and relevant guest result. Treat equality as determinism evidence only.
- [ ] Preserve the discriminators in existing envelope, hidden-envelope, KON preload, directory, terminal BRR, noise, PMON, ordered mixing and echo tests. Recalculate changed expectations only with explicit specification derivations; do not remove cases, skip tests or weaken assertions. Include focused PMON and EON consumers of a changing envelope.
- [ ] Pass Rust checks:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test dsp_envelope_order
cargo test --workspace --locked
```

- [ ] Pass the existing pinned, licensed source-built hardware gates:

```sh
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py \
  --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" \
  --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" \
  --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
```

- [ ] Pass existing fixture and browser regressions, preserving Castle traversal and Memory gameplay/music/effect assertions, source allowlists and expected build hashes:

```sh
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
cd web
npx playwright install chromium
npm test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
```

- [ ] Record actual commands, results, failures and limitations before merge. No commercial ROM/firmware acquisition or downloaded game binaries are required.
- [ ] Preserve all 24 supplied inventory scopes: `cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-hires`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-voices`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo` and `dsp-timing` remain partial; `ppu-raster` and `pal` remain unimplemented. Passing these checks establishes neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
